discovery: Time reversal and wavefront shaping of waves in complex scattering media

nominees.name: Mathias Fink
nominees.affiliation: Institut Langevin, ESPCI Paris - PSL, France

subfield: Optics and wave physics of complex media
motivation: Multiple scattering was long regarded as the ultimate barrier to focusing and imaging with waves. Mathias Fink showed with time-reversal mirrors that disorder can be exploited: waves re-emitted in reversed time refocus through complex media, with superresolution beyond the free-space limit. Vellekoop and Mosk (2007) carried this idea to optics, showing that shaping the incident wavefront with a spatial light modulator focuses light through an opaque, strongly scattering layer, turning speckle into a sharp focus. Together these works founded wavefront shaping, a field built on mesoscopic physics such as open eigenchannels and memory effects. It has led to transmission-matrix measurements, imaging through turbid tissue and multimode fibres, deep-brain microscopy, ultrasound therapy, telecommunications and physical optical computing. By turning scattering from a fundamental limitation into a controllable resource, they changed how physicists understand and use waves in disordered media.
